answer: Sybil defences price identity in money, which is borrowable; a stronger lever is calendar time in a real place. Each seat sinks a numbered marble tile in a lagoon tank, edge sealed with walnut-husk oil. Skimmed, not filtered, the tank lets salt and oil oxidation accrue through real weeks of immersion, while audit reads crust mass against the tile engraving. Keys mint overnight, but no purchase speeds a tide: each new identity still needs a tile, a tank slot and the waiting period, while a forged seat earns one share. An attacker pays N tiles, N slots and N calendars for a single yield.
